continuity_scope: Netflix animated-series continuity only, restricted to official Netflix episode metadata for Season 1 Episode 1, “Echoes of Thunder” (24 minutes), and Episode 2, “What Is Done” (25 minutes). The series page’s overarching premise is used only to identify the television-continuity frame. Novels, comics, games, Tales of Xadia tabletop material, other expanded-universe works, and all episodes after S1E2 are excluded.

The Dragon Prince, Netflix animated series, Season 1 Episode 2 “What Is Done” official episode synopsis

coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic figure directly named in the two official episode synopses: King Harrow, Callum, Ezran, Rayla, and Lord Viren. Moonshadow elves, human/elven peoples, the kingdom of Katolis, castle, attack, safety plan, war/peace framing, institutions, magic, creatures, artifacts, and places remain terms/context. The official series tagline describes two human princes and an elven assassin but does not attach those categories to personal names in the selected episode synopses; no named individual is assigned that category by inference.
omissions: All named characters not supplied in the selected S1E1–S1E2 Netflix synopses, including any figure only visible, voiced, or described in untranscribed episode footage/credits.
All later Season 1 and later-season events, including the episode 3+ names and developments displayed on Netflix, and every novel, comic, game, tabletop, and other expanded-universe claim.

Primal-magic sources, spells, artifacts, dragons, detailed war history, named kingdoms/factions beyond Katolis and Moonshadow elves, identities, disability, ethnicity/cultural coding, family/adoption detail not explicit in these synopses, death, violence outcomes, prejudice mechanisms, and magic morality.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, reviews, recaps, unlicensed transcripts, social posts, and adaptation comparison.
uncertainties: Netflix directly names Harrow as king and Callum/Ezran as his sons, but does not state the boys' ages or specify biological, adoptive, or step-family structure. Father-son links are recorded exactly as stated; no adoption/step-parent inference is made.

The S1E1 synopsis says Katolis braces for a Moonshadow-elf attack; the S1E2 synopsis says Rayla corners Callum and Viren offers the king a way to survive it. These summaries do not give an attack outcome, individual culpability, tactical details, a violence event, or a general claim about peoplehood. They are recorded as fictional war-risk context only.

The official series-level premise says two human princes and an elven assassin later team up for peace, but it provides no name mapping in the selected synopsis metadata. It is not used to label Callum, Ezran, or Rayla. Similarly, the official pages do not substantiate disability, ethnic identity, cultural coding, magic system/moral rules, or language/voice performance claims for this narrow pass.
Netflix regional age labels differ (for example, 10+, 16+, or U/A 7+ shown by regional service pages). No age rating is converted into a child-age, suitability, or content-detail claim.
evidence_basis: Official Netflix series and episode metadata, with Wonderstorm used only to confirm that the animated series is a distinct project alongside game and expanded-universe works. No plot claim relies on a non-official source or untranscribed visual/voice evidence.
